name: fresh basil pesto (small jar)
descriptions: Bright green pesto made from fresh basil leaves, grated Parmesan, toasted pine nuts, garlic, olive oil and a touch of lemon.
Freshly blended and jarred — oil-slicked, herb-forward and fragrant.
effects: You scoop a spoonful of vibrant green pesto straight from the jar. The oily, nutty mouthfeel coats your tongue and the basil hits with a sharp, herbaceous lift.
The fat from the olive oil and pine nuts leaves a lingering, satisfying richness rather than a heavy feeling.

name: fresh lemon vinaigrette (bottle)
descriptions: Emulsified vinaigrette of freshly squeezed lemon juice, Dijon, olive oil, and a pinch of honey and herbs.
Light, tangy and bright — made the same day for maximum citrus aroma.
effects: You take a small sip of the vinaigrette; the sharp lemon and mustard tang hit immediately, followed by a clean, oily warmth.
It refreshes the palate more than it fills you, with a lingering citrus acidity.

name: fresh salsa roja (cup)
descriptions: Chopped ripe tomatoes, onions, cilantro, jalapeño, lime and salt — freshly made and still bright.
Chunky, juicy and slightly spicy, with a strong tomato-lime freshness.
effects: You taste a spoonful of fresh salsa: juicy tomato shards burst, lime brightens the heat and the cilantro adds a green snap.
The high water content is lively on the tongue — refreshing, slightly spicy and satisfying.

name: whole grain mustard
descriptions: Coarsely ground mustard seeds, vinegar, a little honey and spices — tangy with a textured bite.
Freshly made with a pronounced mustard seed aroma and gentle heat.
effects: You swallow a small dab of whole grain mustard; the initial vinegary tang and percussive mustard heat open your sinuses.
It doesn't fill you much but leaves a sharp, lingering spice on the tongue.

name: roasted garlic olive-oil dip (jar)
descriptions: Slow-roasted garlic mashed into extra-virgin olive oil with a pinch of sea salt and lemon zest.
Creamy in texture from the garlic puree and glossy with olive oil.
effects: You take a spoonful: the roasted garlic is mellow and sweet, the oil carries it luxuriously across your mouth.
It's rich and savory, leaving a warm, lingering oiliness rather than immediate fullness.

name: chimichurri (small jar)
descriptions: Vibrant Argentinian sauce of chopped parsley, oregano, garlic, red wine vinegar and olive oil.
Fresh-herb forward, tangy and a little garlicky — made the same day for a green punch.
effects: You taste a spoonful of chimichurri: an herbaceous wave with sharp garlic and vinegar bite, finishing on a grassy olive-oil note.
It livens the mouth and appetite more than it fills you, leaving a bright, lingering herbiness.

name: tahini sauce (jar)
descriptions: Smooth sesame paste thinned with lemon juice, water, and a touch of garlic — nutty, creamy and earthy.
Freshly whisked tahini sauce with a glossy, slightly viscous texture.
effects: You take a spoonful of tahini: dense, nutty sesame flavors coat your mouth and leave a slightly bitter, satisfying finish.
The high oil and seed content feels substantial and caloric rather than watery.

name: gochujang (fermented chili paste)
descriptions: Korean fermented chili paste made from red chili, glutinous rice, fermented soy, and salt — sweet, spicy, umami-rich.
Freshly stirred, with a glossy deep red color and balanced heat.
effects: You sample a fingertip of gochujang: immediate savory umami, a slow-building sweetness, then warm chili heat that lingers.
It's intensely flavored so a little goes a long way — warming and appetite-stirring.

name: quick pickled cucumber slices
descriptions: Thinly sliced cucumbers flash-pickled in vinegar, sugar, salt and dill — crunchy, tangy and bright.
Made the same day so the cucumbers remain crisp and juicy.
effects: You pop a slice into your mouth: the crisp cucumber crunch gives way to sharp vinegar and a dill perfume.
It's refreshing and lightly filling, with a clean, tangy finish.

name: fresh tzatziki (cup)
descriptions: Thick strained yogurt mixed with grated cucumber, garlic, lemon juice and fresh dill — creamy, cooling and herby.
Made from fresh yogurt and cucumbers, stirred lightly to preserve texture.
effects: You taste a spoonful of tzatziki: cool yogurt soothes, cucumber freshness lifts and a gentle garlic tang plays in the background.
It's both cooling and modestly satisfying, leaving a clean, slightly tangy aftertaste.

name: Assorted Condiment Pack
descriptions: A compact cardboard sleeve holding an assortment of single-serve sauce sachets and small cups — perfect for takeout or a picnic.
Includes a mix of ketchup, mustard, mayo, soy sauce, hot sauce, BBQ sauce, ranch, and honey packets arranged in an easy-tear tray.

name: Ketchup Sachet
descriptions: A tear-open sachet of classic tomato ketchup, thick and slightly sweet.
Designed to be squeezed onto fries, burgers, or used as a quick dip.
effects: You squeeze the ketchup straight from the sachet — sweet, vinegary tomato paste coats your tongue and brings a familiar savory comfort.
A small, satisfying dollop makes fried snacks taste noticeably richer.

name: Yellow Mustard Packet
descriptions: A thin packet of tangy yellow mustard with a sharp, vinegary bite.
Brightens sandwiches and sausages with a punch of mustard seed flavor.
effects: You tear and squeeze the mustard; the fierce, tangy heat wakes up your palate and adds a bright note to anything it touches.
A sting of acidity lingers, making fatty bites feel lighter.

name: Mayonnaise Cup
descriptions: A small sealed cup of creamy mayonnaise — rich and slightly tangy.
Thick texture meant for spreading or dipping; a little goes a long way.
effects: You scoop a spoonful of mayo and taste a dense, fatty creaminess that clings to the mouth.
The richness makes light snacks feel indulgent but can leave a lingering oily coating.

name: Soy Sauce Mini Bottle
descriptions: A tiny plastic bottle of dark, salty soy sauce with umami depth.
Often included with sushi or noodles; provides a salty-savory boost in small doses.
effects: You tip a drop onto your tongue — an immediate wave of salty, fermented umami that amplifies savory notes.
A little goes a long way; it makes bland foods taste markedly more complex.

name: Hot Sauce Sachet
descriptions: A small packet of fiery hot sauce with chili heat and vinegar tang.
Ideal for adding spice to snacks or a quick kick to bland food.
effects: You tear and taste the hot sauce; bright vinegar and capsaicin scorch the tip of your tongue and bring a flush of heat.
The spice can be exhilarating and makes other flavors pop, leaving a warm afterglow.

name: BBQ Sauce Cup
descriptions: A small plastic cup filled with smoky-sweet barbecue sauce.
Notes of molasses, smoke, and tomato create a sticky glaze perfect for grilled things.
effects: You dip a fry into the BBQ sauce; the smoky-sweet syrup coats each bite and lends a grill-char warmth.
The sugar and spices make savory snacks feel heartier, with a pleasant sticky finish.

name: Ranch Dressing Cup
descriptions: A pale, creamy cup of ranch dressing — herb-forward with a garlicky tang.
A classic dip for vegetables, chips, or chicken fingers.
effects: You taste the ranch straight from the cup; cool, herby, and garlicky cream slips across the palate and smooths spicy or salty bites.
Its richness makes raw veggies feel more indulgent.

name: Honey Packet
descriptions: A slender tear-strip packet of pure honey — sticky, floral, and very sweet.
Used to sweeten tea or drizzle over bread and snacks; easy to carry and squeeze.
effects: You squeeze a strip of honey into your mouth; it clings thickly, floods your tongue with concentrated floral sugar, and leaves a warm, lingering sweetness.
Instant energy from the sugars and a soothing coat in the throat if taken slowly.

name: bottle of ketchup
descriptions: A squeezable plastic bottle filled with thick, sweet-tangy tomato ketchup.
Commonly used as a tabletop condiment; the cap has a small dispensing hole and residue often clings to the rim.
effects: You squeeze a dollop of ketchup directly into your mouth: the sweetness and vinegar hit immediately, leaving a sticky coating on your tongue.
The thick texture makes each bite feel more substantial than its calories imply.

name: jar of mustard
descriptions: A small glass jar of yellow mustard with a sharp, vinegary aroma.
Bright and tangy, it’s sold sealed and keeps for a long time once unopened.
effects: You scoop a spoonful of mustard and taste an immediate mustard heat and vinegar tang that clears the sinuses.
The pungent bite lingers, adding a sharp note to anything eaten afterward.

name: bottle of soy sauce
descriptions: A dark glass bottle of fermented soy sauce, intensely salty with umami depth.
A little goes a long way; the aroma is savory and slightly fermented.
effects: You tip a few drops of soy sauce into your mouth: a concentrated hit of salt and umami floods the palate.
The strong savoury note can make you crave something bland or plain to balance it.

name: jar of mayonnaise
descriptions: A creamy jar of mayonnaise: rich, thick, and oily with a subtle tang.
High in fat and calories, commonly used as a spread or base for dressings.
effects: You take a spoonful of mayonnaise; the mouthfeel is luxuriously fatty and smooth, leaving an oily coating.
It feels filling despite being paste-like, and its neutral flavor amplifies other tastes you eat afterward.

name: bottle of hot sauce
descriptions: A small bottle of bright red hot sauce with chili oil floating on top.
Spicy and vinegary, designed to add heat to dishes in small amounts.
effects: You swallow a teardrop of hot sauce: a sharp, immediate burn spreads across your tongue and throat, followed by a lingering warmth.
The vinegar brightens the heat, leaving a tingling after-sensation.

name: jar of pickles
descriptions: A glass jar of preserved cucumber spears in a brine of vinegar, water, and spices.
Crunchy and tart, the brine keeps them shelf-stable until opened.
effects: You bite into a pickle straight from the jar: the crunch is juicy and sharp, the vinegar tang wakes the mouth.
The salty-briny flavor is refreshing and slightly effervescent on the tongue.

name: jar of chutney
descriptions: A thick, sweet-spicy chutney made from reduced fruit, vinegar, sugar, and spices.
Sticky and aromatic, it pairs well with cheeses and grilled meats.
effects: You taste a spoonful of chutney: candied fruit sweetness arrives first, followed by warm spice notes and a gentle acidity.
The texture is sticky and clinging, leaving a fruity aftertaste.

name: tube of tomato paste
descriptions: A small metal tube of concentrated tomato paste; dense, intensely flavored, and slightly sticky.
Used in small amounts to thicken and deepen tomato flavor in sauces and stews.
effects: You squeeze a pea-sized blob of tomato paste into your mouth: an intense, concentrated tomato savor overwhelms the palate with a slightly earthy tang.
The thick paste clings and leaves a lingering tomato intensity.

name: bottle of barbecue sauce
descriptions: A BBQ sauce bottle—sweet, smoky, and vinegary with a molasses-like thickness.
Commonly used for glazing grilled foods; it has a sticky, caramelized flavor profile.
effects: You spoon a taste of barbecue sauce: a smoky sweetness with caramel notes and a mild tang coats the mouth.
The sugary undertone makes it feel indulgent and slightly sticky on the lips.

name: Fresh Herb Bouquet
descriptions: A small tied bundle of fresh culinary herbs — basil, parsley, and cilantro — harvested within the last day.
Bright green, fragrant leaves with a crisp, slightly peppery bite. Ideal for garnishing or eating raw for a fresh hit of flavor.
effects: You bite a tender sprig; the leaves crush easily, releasing a grassy, bright aroma and a burst of green, slightly peppery flavor.
Eating the bouquet raw refreshes your mouth like a salad garnish — cooling and lively rather than filling.

name: Saffron Threads
descriptions: A tiny sachet of vivid red saffron threads — delicate stigmas with a floral, honeyed scent.
Extremely aromatic and prized; each thread is light but powerfully fragrant.
effects: You chew a few raw threads; a floral, slightly metallic sweetness blooms across your tongue and leaves a lingering golden aroma.
The taste is intense and ephemeral — aromatic more than filling, like inhaling a perfume with edible texture.

name: Grains of Paradise (jar)
descriptions: A small glass jar of peppery, citrus-tinged Grains of Paradise — tiny brown seeds with a warm, complex bite.
Used like a pepper substitute with a brighter, spicier profile and subtle orange notes.
effects: You pop a couple of seeds into your mouth; a compact explosion of peppery warmth and citrus lifts the palate.
They leave a gentle heat and a clear, bright spiciness that wakes your senses without weighing you down.

name: Star Anise (whole pods)
descriptions: Whole star-shaped pods with crisp, woody shells and concentrated anise (licorice) flavor.
Aromatic and decorative; typically used whole in steeping or slow cooking but edible if chewed carefully.
effects: You chew a pod; a strong licorice-like sweetness and astringent backbone wash across your tongue with a pleasant warming quality.
The experience is aromatic and slightly drying — flavorful and memorable rather than filling.

name: Black Cardamom Pods
descriptions: Large, smoky black cardamom pods with bold, resinous, camphor-like notes — used for deep, savory applications.
Robust and smoky compared to green cardamom; whole pods contain seeds that can be chewed for concentrated flavor.
effects: You bite a pod and crush the seeds; an intense, smoky menthol warmth fills your mouth with a resinous, almost medicinal kick.
The taste is powerful and energizing — clearly aromatic and more stimulating than filling.

name: Cinnamon Bark Sticks
descriptions: A short bundle of dried cinnamon bark sticks — sweet, woody, and warmly aromatic.
Chewing a stick releases fragrant oils that are sweet and warming; commonly used for infusions and as a chewable palate cleanser.
effects: You gnaw a piece of bark; a comforting sweet warmth and a little astringency coat your mouth, like a dry, spiced candy.
The fibers give a slight chew while the oils uplift your mood and give a gentle warming buzz.

name: Sumac Powder (paper pouch)
descriptions: A small paper pouch of deep red sumac powder — tart, lemony, and bright.
Often used as a souring spice; dry and flaky with a tang that lifts rich dishes.
effects: You lick a pinch of powder; a sudden, pleasant tartness floods your mouth like concentrated lemon zest.
The sour spike is refreshing and vivid — it wakes the palate and leaves a dry, zesty aftertaste.

name: Vanilla Bean Pod
descriptions: A single dark vanilla bean pod with sticky interior seeds and a deep, sweet floral aroma.
Typically scraped for its seeds, the whole pod can be chewed for a concentrated vanilla experience.
effects: You split the pod and scrape or chew it; sticky seeds and fragrant oils coat your mouth with a warm, complex sweetness.
The sensation is indulgent and aromatic, like a tiny mouthful of dessert spice rather than substantial food.

name: Bundle of Fresh Spices (Assortment)
descriptions: A wrapped set of small jars and packets containing staple spices: sea salt, black peppercorns, ground cinnamon, smoked paprika, and ground cumin. Packaged with a small fresh-herb sprig.
Designed for gifting or starter pantry kits — lightweight, stackable, and sealed. The jars are labeled and arranged in a recycled cardboard sleeve.
effects: You pinch a tiny sample of each spice and taste them one after another: briny salt that makes your mouth water, a sharp hit of pepper that makes you cough and clear your sinuses, warm cinnamon that tickles the tongue, a smoky paprika whisper, and an earthy cumin aftertaste.
The fresh-herb sprig adds a fleeting green brightness when chewed raw, while the concentrated dried powders leave your mouth feeling dry and slightly tingly.

name: Jar of Sea Salt
descriptions: A small glass jar of coarse sea salt crystals. Useful for cooking and finishing dishes.
The crystals are dry and crunch when handled; a single pinch is intensely salty.
effects: You pop a few salt crystals onto your tongue — an immediate, overwhelming saline bite that makes your mouth pucker and leaves you thirsty.
Eating salt raw is sharp and abrasive; it can sting tiny mouth abrasions and quickly make you want a drink.

name: Black Peppercorn Jar
descriptions: A small jar of whole black peppercorns. They can be used whole, cracked, or ground with a mill.
Crunchy and aromatic when chewed; the flavor is spicy and pungent.
effects: You chew a peppercorn: a sharp, biting heat builds in your nose and throat, making you cough and sneeze a little while your eyes water.
The bite clears your sinuses briefly and leaves a warm, tingling sensation in the mouth.

name: Ground Cinnamon Tin
descriptions: A small tin of fragrant ground cinnamon. Sweet, woody aroma when opened.
Very dry and fine powder; a little dust clouds the air when the tin is shaken.
effects: You taste a pinch of dry cinnamon straight from the tin — a burst of warm sweetness followed by a dry, slightly mouth-coating sensation that can make you cough if you inhale any dust.
It leaves a lingering warming sensation on the tongue and throat.

name: Smoked Paprika Jar
descriptions: A compact jar of smoked paprika: vibrant red, smoky, and mildly sweet.
Adds color and a smoky note to dishes; the powder is fine and lightly oily to the touch.
effects: You taste a small pinch of smoked paprika — a gentle smoky sweetness that lingers on the palate without being overpowering.
The powder is pleasantly aromatic, giving a sense of warmth rather than sharp heat.

name: Ground Cumin
descriptions: A little jar of ground cumin with a deep, earthy aroma and slightly bitter undertones.
Highly aromatic when sniffed; the powder is fine and can stick slightly to moist skin.
effects: You let a crumb of cumin rest on your tongue — an earthy, warm bitterness that grows into a savory backbone flavor, leaving an herbal aftertaste.
It feels grounding and aromatic, not particularly filling.

name: Fresh Herb Bundle (Basil & Parsley)
descriptions: A small tied bunch of fresh basil leaves and curly parsley. Bright green, aromatic, and slightly moist from recent harvesting.
Best used quickly; can be chewed raw for a burst of fresh, grassy flavor.
effects: You chew a leaf of basil followed by a sprig of parsley — cooling, peppery notes from the basil and a crisp, slightly bitter freshness from the parsley.
The fresh herbs are pleasant to eat raw and leave your mouth feeling refreshed.

name: Wooden Spice Rack (Compact)
descriptions: A small wall-mountable wooden spice rack designed to hold six small jars. Sturdy recycled pine with labeled slots.
Useful for organizing a starter spice bundle; it is static once mounted and not intended to be stacked.
